display.pairHint: Enter the pairing code from Counter Pay → Displays.
display.pairWrong: That code didn't match. Try again.
display.pairWait: Too many tries. Wait a minute.

popup.hint: Enter to show · Esc to cancel
popup.displayOffline: Display not connected · shown on simulator
popup.noPayee: Set up the payee in Counter Pay first

toast.upToDate: Counter Pay is up to date
toast.updateAfterQr: Clear the QR first, then update

home.noShop: Set your shop name in Content
home.noPayee: No payee yet. Import your merchant standee QR to show QRs.
home.noDisplays: No display is on. Turn one on in Displays.
home.notPayments: What was shown, not what was paid. Your UPI merchant app or bank stays the record of payments.
home.shortcutHint: They work from any window, including your billing software. Change them in Settings.
home.lockTestNone: Not done yet. First-run setup includes it.

history.lead: Every QR shown on a customer display.

displays.lead: Any screen the customer can see. Every display shows the same scene.
displays.addWindow: A second screen plugged into this PC (HDMI, USB-C or a small LCD).
displays.addWeb: A phone, tablet or old laptop on the shop Wi-Fi. No new hardware.
displays.addUsb: An E-ink panel on an ESP32 board, plugged in by USB.
displays.phase2: USB colour displays arrive in a later release.
displays.usbLooking: Looking for the board. Plug it in by USB; it says hello when it starts.
displays.addWifi: An E-ink panel on a Raspberry Pi or other board on the shop network.
displays.wifiLooking: Looking for the display on the network (last seen at {{address}}). Check it is on and on the same network as this PC.
displays.wifiUnpaired: The display no longer knows this PC: it was reset or paired with another PC. Remove it and pair it again.

wifi.title: Pair a Wi-Fi display
wifi.lead: Start Counter Pay on the display: its screen shows a 6-digit code. It must be on the same network as this PC.
wifi.none: None found yet. Check the display is on and on the same network, or enter its name or address below (shown on its screen, for example raspberrypi.local).
wifi.pairedElsewhere: Paired with another PC: reset it first

error.code: That code doesn't match the one on the display. After 5 wrong tries the display shows a new code.
error.paired: This display is paired with another PC. Reset it first (see HARDWARE.md).
error.key: This display is paired with another PC. Reset it first (see HARDWARE.md).
error.busy: The display is busy. Try again in a moment.
error.unreachable: Couldn't reach it. Check the address and that it's on the same network as this PC.
error.address: That doesn't look like an address. Use a name like raspberrypi.local or an address like 192.168.1.20.

displays.usbPanelSilent: The board is on {{port}}, but its panel isn't drawing. Check the wires to the panel, especially VCC, GND and BUSY (see HARDWARE.md).
displays.usbFirmware: Not found? Flash the Counter Pay firmware first (see HARDWARE.md), and close any other program using the port, like the Arduino serial monitor.
displays.simulatorHint: Shows the customer screen in a window on this PC, for trying Counter Pay before buying hardware.
displays.plugIn: Plug in a second monitor first. Counter Pay never covers the cashier's own screen.
displays.noNetwork: This PC isn't on a network.

content.lead: What customers see between payments, and on the Thanks screen.
content.logoSlide: Your logo and a welcome line.
content.standeeSlide: Your standee QR with no amount, under your shop name: the customer types the amount. Add a message below, such as "Happy Shopping!".
content.noLogo: No logo yet: the shop name is shown instead.
content.thanksHint: After Clear. It shows the rating QR when you have added one.

settings.clearHint: Removes the QR without opening anything.
settings.expiryHint: A QR nobody cleared goes away on its own.
settings.maxHint: Amounts above {{max}} are refused, to catch an extra zero.
settings.mamHint: Only if the amount-lock test showed it helps.
settings.startAtLoginHint: Counter Pay waits in the tray, ready for the shortcut.
settings.apiHint: For point-of-sale apps and scripts on this PC. The API arrives in Phase 3.
settings.backupHint: Save or restore all settings as a file.
settings.portHint: Takes effect after Counter Pay restarts.
settings.logsHint: If something goes wrong, the log file shows what happened. Attach it when reporting a problem.

payee.drop: Drop a photo or screenshot of your standee QR
payee.dropHint: Or click to choose a file, or paste a screenshot (Ctrl+V).
payee.noQr: No QR code found in that picture. Try a sharper, closer photo.

issue.notUpi: That isn't a UPI payment QR.
issue.noPayee: That QR has no UPI ID (pa).

payee.signed: This QR is signed. Adding an amount may stop some apps accepting it: run the amount-lock test before relying on it.
payee.label: Name shown to customers
payee.labelHint: Shown as "Paying: …" so customers can match the name their UPI app shows.

shortcut.same: Show and Clear need different keys.
shortcut.refused: Windows wouldn't let Counter Pay use {{key}}. Pick another key.

warning.reservedF12: Windows reserves {{key}} for debuggers, so it can't be a shortcut. Try F9.
warning.layoutSwitch: {{key}} switches keyboard layouts (Tamil input). Pick another key.
warning.windowMenu: {{key}} opens the window menu. Pick another key.
warning.needsKey: Press a key, not just Ctrl, Alt or Shift.
warning.plainKey: {{key}} on its own would stop that key typing in your billing software. Use a function key or add Ctrl or Alt.

meaning.locked: Customers' apps can't change the amount on your QR.
meaning.editable: The preset amount still stops most casual short-paying. Keep "goods after full payment".
meaning.mixed: Some apps let customers edit it. Check the amount in your payment alerts for those.

setup.payeeLead: Counter Pay builds every QR from your real merchant standee QR, so money always goes to the same account.
setup.shortcutsLead: Press the keys you want. They work while your billing software has focus.
setup.shortcutsNote: Try each one in your billing software first, so nothing collides.
setup.displayLead: Pick one to start. You can add more later in Displays.

choice.simulatorHint: A window on this screen. Good for trying the workflow.
choice.windowHint: A second screen facing the customer.
choice.web: A phone or tablet on Wi-Fi
choice.webHint: Open a web page on it and enter a code.

setup.testLead: A ₹1 QR is now on your display. This checks whether customers' apps can change a fixed amount.
setup.testStep1: Scan it with two or three UPI apps (GPay, PhonePe, Paytm).
setup.testStep2: Look at the amount before paying. Try to change it.
setup.testStep3: Pay ₹1 once and check that it reaches your account (merchant app, bank SMS or payment speaker).
setup.testWaiting: Putting the QR on your display…
setup.question: Could you change the amount?
setup.languageLabel: Second language on the customer display
setup.languageHint: English is always shown. Change this any time in Content.

update.title: Updates

status.disabled: Updates work in the installed app, not in a development build.
status.ready: v{{version}} is ready. It installs in quiet hours, or when you quit.

update.quietHint: A downloaded update installs by itself in these hours when no QR is showing. It never restarts during billing.
update.whatsNew: Counter Pay was updated to v{{version}}.

server.localPortBusy: Counter Pay could not start its display server: port {{port}} is in use. Change the port in Settings → Advanced, then restart Counter Pay.
server.lanPortBusy: Phone and tablet displays are unavailable: port {{port}} is in use. Change the Wi-Fi port in Settings → Advanced, then restart Counter Pay.
